title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East  (Late Show) on 1970-05-15
lineage: 10 inch 1/2 track Master Reels @ 7.5 ips > Revox A700 > Alesis Masterlink ML 9600 > CD

ai_review.summary: Crisp soundboard capture of the marathon May 15 1970 double‑show, with monster versions of The Other One, Dark Star and a killer New Riders set.
ai_review.review: The recording is a well‑preserved sound‑board tape that sounds clear and balanced for most of the show, though the early acoustic portion suffers from occasional right‑channel drop‑outs and a vocal level that runs hot. Musically this is a landmark 1970 performance – two full sets plus New Riders – featuring scorching renditions of The Other One, Dark Star, Attics, Good Lovin’, Candyman and an unforgettable NRPS set. Reviewers rave about the energy, the rare song choices and the historic length, making it one of the most celebrated shows from that era.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews overwhelmingly positive about the performance; recording is generally praised with only minor technical quirks, yielding a strong combined score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp mix and minimal hiss overall. Early acoustic set has right‑channel fade‑ins/out, occasional vocal level excess, and a patched segment in St. Stephen due to missing reel. No major distortion; stereo restoration of Candyman noted as a treat.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Two‑show marathon (early + late) with two acoustic sets, a New Riders middle set and two electric halves; the pacing is praised for its epic length yet cohesive flow, delivering rare cuts and classic jams.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for fierce guitar work on The Other One and Dark Star; described as "game on" and "fierce".
band_member_comments.Phil: Mentioned only once – a reviewer couldn’t hear him, indicating the mix down‑played his bass.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted sitting in with NRPS on “Mama Tried” and other songs; generally positive but not heavily discussed.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ and vocals are highlighted as clear and strong (not drunk); keyboards receive special mention for their presence.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s intro called out as fun; Mickey Hart’s brush work noted on acoustic numbers.
